'''Koa Seward Peat''' (born January 20, 2007) is a professional American [[basketball]] player for the [[Phoenix Suns]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]]. A consensus [[five-star recruit]], he was one of the top-ranked players of the 2025 class.

==High school career==
Peat attended [[Perry High School (Gilbert, Arizona)|Perry High School]] in [[Gilbert, Arizona]]. He joined the varsity basketball team in June 2021.<ref name="prized">{{cite news |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2021/06/04/prized-2025-basketball-prospect-koa-peat-joining-perry/7548661002/ |title=Prized 6-foot-7 2025 basketball phenom Koa Peat joining Perry High School |work=[[The Arizona Republic]] |first=Richard |last=Obert |date=June 4, 2021 |access-date=May 10, 2023}}</ref><ref name="azcentral">{{cite news|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2022/04/21/perrys-koa-peat-rated-no-2-overall-nationally-2025-class-espn/7397483001/|title=ESPN's No. 2 basketball prospect in 2025 class is from Arizona|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]|first=Richard|last=Obert|date=April 21, 2022|access-date=May 9, 2023}}</ref> His head coach, Sam Duane Jr., had previously coached two of his older brothers to state titles at [[Corona del Sol High School]] in nearby [[Tempe, Arizona|Tempe]].<ref name=prized/> As a freshman at Perry, Peat averaged 15 [[Point (basketball)|points]], 6.1 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebound]]s, 1.6 [[Assist (basketball)|assist]]s and 1.8 [[Block (basketball)|blocks]] per game and teamed with [[Cody Williams]] to guide the Pumas to their first-ever Class 6A state championship.<ref name=azcentral/> He recorded 14 points, six rebounds and two blocks in the 48–38 title game victory over [[Hamilton High School (Chandler, Arizona)|Hamilton]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2022/03/02/cody-williams-koa-peat-lead-perry-first-state-basketball-title/9354909002/|title=Cody Williams, Koa Peat lead Perry to first state basketball title with win over Hamilton|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]|first=Richard|last=Obert|date=March 2, 2022|access-date=May 9, 2023}}</ref>

As a sophomore, Peat averaged 19.7 points, 9.4 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 1.7 blocks and 1.3 steals per game on 70 percent shooting while leading the Pumas to a 30–1 record and the inaugural [[Arizona Interscholastic Association|AIA]] Open Division state title.<ref name="maxpreps">{{cite news|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/OZRmg0z-20-PdHXxpbfiIQ/koa-peat-named-2022-23-maxpreps-arizona-high-school-basketball-player-of-the-year.htm|title=Koa Peat named 2022-23 MaxPreps Arizona High School Basketball Player of the Year|work=[[MaxPreps]]|first=Jordan|last=Divens|date=March 9, 2023|access-date=May 9, 2023}}</ref><ref name="title">{{cite news|url=https://www.eastvalleytribune.com/sports/perry-wins-first-open-division-basketball-championship-over-sunnyslope/article_26ba2e70-bb03-11ed-92a4-7b4498ff9c2e.html|title=Perry wins first Open Division basketball championship over Sunnyslope|work=[[East Valley Tribune]]|first=Zach|last=Alvira|date=March 4, 2023|access-date=May 9, 2023}}</ref> In the championship game, he recorded a basketball: Koa Peat goes off for 35 points as No. 15 Perry wins second consecutive Arizona title|work=[[MaxPreps]]|first=Jordan|last=Divens|date=March 4, 2023|access-date=May 9, 2023}}</ref> Peat was named the Arizona [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] and the [[MaxPreps]] Arizona Player of the Year.<ref name=maxpreps/><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2023/03/15/perrys-koa-peat-named-gatorade-arizona-hs-basketball-player-of-year/70011847007/|title=Perry 6-8 sophomore named Gatorade Arizona HS Basketball Player of the Year|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]|first=Richard|last=Obert|date=March 15, 2023|access-date=May 9, 2023}}</ref>

As a junior, Peat averaged 20.5 points, 10.6 rebounds, 3.4 assists, 2.2 blocks and 1.0 steals per game, leading Perry to a 25–6 record and another AIA Open Division state title,{{ efn | Gatorade incorrectly reports Perry's record as 24–6. }} as well as their third-straight state crown overall.<ref name="maxpreps1">{{cite news|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/2fSw_C0auk-wiPPmXo93cg/koa-peat-named-2023-24-arizona-maxpreps-high-school-basketball-player-of-the-year.htm|title=Koa Peat named 2023-24 Arizona MaxPreps High School Basketball Player of the Year|work=[[MaxPreps]]|first=Jordan|last=Divens|date=March 5, 2024|access-date=November 3, 2025}}</ref><ref name="Gatorade">{{cite news|url=https://playeroftheyear.gatorade.com/winner/koa-peat/40211|title=Koa Peat Gatorade 2023 - 2024 Player of the Year Boys Basketball - Arizona|publisher=[[Gatorade]]|date=March 21, 2024|access-date=November 3, 2025}}</ref> In the championship game, he posted 21 points, 13 rebounds and four assists to help the Pumas overcome a 17-point deficit in an eventual 71–67 win over [[Millennium High School (Arizona)|Millennium]].<ref name=maxpreps1/> Peat repeated as the Arizona Gatorade Player of the Year and the MaxPreps Arizona Player of the Year.<ref name=maxpreps1/><ref name=Gatorade/>

As a senior, Peat averaged 18.7 points, 10.3 rebounds, 5.1 assists, 1.6 blocks and 1.0 steals per game, leading Perry to a 27–2 record,{{ efn | Gatorade incorrectly reports Perry's record as 26–2. }} a third straight AIA Open Division state title, and a fourth straight state title overall.<ref name="cement">{{cite news|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2025/03/08/perry-cements-dynasty-with-4th-straight-boys-basketball-title/81173645007/|title=Koa Peat, Perry cement Arizona high school basketball dynasty with 4th straight title|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]|first=Richard|last=Obert|date=March 8, 2025|access-date=November 4, 2025}}</ref><ref name="Gatorade1">{{cite news|url=https://playeroftheyear.gatorade.com/winner/koa-peat/40872|title=Koa Peat Gatorade 2024 - 2025 Player of the Year Boys Basketball - Arizona|publisher=[[Gatorade]]|date=March 20, 2025|access-date=November 4, 2025}}</ref> Despite suffering a broken right hand in practice two days before the state quarterfinals, he returned for the semifinals, where he scored 16 points in a 76–57 win over [[Sandra Day O'Connor High School (Arizona)|Sandra Day O'Connor]], before recording 20 points, nine rebounds and two blocks in a 63–44 win over Sunnyslope in the championship game.<ref name=cement/><ref name="maxpreps2">{{cite news|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/DpWexcJmC0-m8Mh0y70tFA/koa-peat-named-2024-25-arizona-maxpreps-high-school-basketball-player-of-the-year.htm|title=Koa Peat named 2024-25 Arizona MaxPreps High School Basketball Player of the Year|work=[[MaxPreps]]|first=Jordan|last=Divens|date=March 12, 2025|access-date=November 4, 2025}}</ref> Peat was named the Arizona Gatorade Player of the Year and the MaxPreps Arizona Player of the Year for the third year in a row.<ref name=Gatorade1/><ref name=maxpreps2/> He was selected to both the [[2025 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]] and the [[Nike Hoop Summit]], but was unable to play in either due to undergoing surgery for his broken hand.<ref name="NLI">{{cite news|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2025/04/16/koa-peat-arizona-basketball-signing-day/83122975007/|title=Perry's Koa Peat officially signs with Arizona Wildcats basketball|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]|first=Richard|last=Obert|date=April 16, 2025|access-date=November 4, 2025}}</ref>

===Recruiting===
Peat was a consensus five-star [[College recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2025 class, according to major recruiting services. He received his first scholarship offer from [[NCAA Division I]] program [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]] as an eighth grader and a second from [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]] before starting high school.<ref name=prized/><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2021/02/08/asu-basketball-extends-offer-6-7-8th-grader-koa-peat/4443903001/|title=Arizona State basketball extends offer to 6-7 8th-grade phenom Koa Peat|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]|first=Richard|last=Obert|date=February 8, 2021|access-date=May 10, 2023}}</ref>

On March 27, 2025, Peat announced his commitment to play [[college basketball]] at the [[University of Arizona]] during a live appearance on [[The Pat McAfee Show]] on [[ESPN]]. His top five schools also included Arizona State, Baylor, Houston and Texas.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://cronkitenews.azpbs.org/2025/03/27/perry-high-koa-peat-picks-arizona-over-asu/|title=Staying home: Perry High All-American Koa Peat picks Arizona over ASU, Houston, Baylor and Texas|work=[[Cronkite News]]|first=Dan|last=Allison|date=March 27, 2025|access-date=November 3, 2025}}</ref> Peat officially signed his [[National Letter of Intent]] on April 16.<ref name=NLI/>

==College career==
Peat made his [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|collegiate]] debut on November 3, 2025, leading all scorers with 30 points along with seven rebounds, five assists, three steals and a block in a nationally televised 93–87 [[upset win]] over No. 3 [[2025–26 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]], the defending national champions.<ref>{{cite web |title=Freshman Koa Peat leads Arizona past reigning NCAA champion Florida |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/46839888 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=November 3, 2025 |access-date=November 4, 2025|others=Contributed by ESPN Research and The Associated Press}}</ref> He led Arizona to both the [[Big 12]] regular-season championship and tournament championship, which earned his team a 1-seed for the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. He scored 20 points in the [[Elite Eight]] against [[2025–26 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]] to help send the team to the [[Final Four]] for the first time in 25 years.<ref>{{cite news |last=Jerome |first=Ryder |title=Koa Peat leads Arizona to first Final Four under Lloyd |url=https://www.tucsonspotlight.org/koa-peat-leads-arizona-to-first-final-four-under-lloyd/ |access-date=April 22, 2026 |work=Tucson Spotlight |date=April 2, 2026}}</ref> Following the end of the season, Peat, alongside his teammates [[Brayden Burries]] and [[Jaden Bradley]], entered the [[2026 NBA draft]] on April 24, 2026.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Arizona forward Koa Peat posts official declaration for NBA Draft
|url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/article_6d3de173-4551-43b3-b72f-af4d401910b7.html
 |website=[[Arizona Daily Star]]
 |access-date=May 13, 2026
|date=April 24, 2026|last=Pascoe|first=Bruce}}</ref>

==Professional career==
On June 23, 2026, Peat was selected by the [[Dallas Mavericks]] with the 30th overall pick in the [[2026 NBA draft]], but was subsequently traded to the [[New York Knicks]] and then to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in exchange for [[Sergio de Larrea]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/breaking-news/article/nba-draft-suns-trade-up-to-select-arizona-star-koa-peat-at-no-30-in-deal-with-mavericks-knicks-033825540.html|title=NBA Draft: Suns trade up to select Arizona star Koa Peat at No. 30 in deal with Mavericks, Knicks|website=Yahoo Sports|last=Young|first=Ryan|date=June 24, 2026|access-date=July 15, 2026}}</ref>

==National team career==
Peat won a gold medal with the [[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|United States national under-17 team]] at the [[2022 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup|2022 FIBA Under-17 World Cup]] in Spain, earning [[FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup All-Tournament Team|all-tournament team]] honors after averaging 9.6 points, 4.3 rebounds and 1.4 assists per game.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.on3.com/news/koa-peat-discusses-latest-offers-and-recent-visit-arizona-arizona-state-baylor-stanford-lsu/|title=5-star Koa Peat discusses latest offers and recent visit|work=[[On3.com]]|first=Jamie|last=Shaw|date=October 15, 2022|access-date=May 10, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Koa-Peat/Summary/180367|title=Koa Peat|publisher=[[RealGM]]|access-date=May 10, 2023}}</ref> He helped the team to another gold at the [[2023 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship]] in Mexico after averaging a team-high 17.2 points to go with 8.3 rebounds and 3.2 assists per game—which included a 29-point, 14-rebound performance against [[Puerto Rico men's national under-16 basketball team|Puerto Rico]] in the semifinal—and was named the 2023 [[USA Basketball Male Athlete of the Year]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.usab.com/news/2023/11/koa-peat-earns-male-athlete-of-the-year-award-through-continued-growth-impressive-leadership|title=Koa Peat Earns Male Athlete of the Year Award Through Continued Growth, Impressive Leadership|publisher=[[USA Basketball]]|first=Tristan|last=Tucker|date=November 30, 2023|access-date=January 10, 2026}}</ref> Peat became the first player to win multiple gold medals at the [[FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup|FIBA Under-17 World Cup]] when he helped the U.S. to another first-place finish at the [[2024 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup|2024 edition]] in Turkey. He averaged 17.9 points, 5.6 rebounds and 2.1 assists per game and scored 26 points in their 129–88 win over [[Italy men's national under-17 basketball team|Italy]] in the final.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://eu.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2024/07/07/perrys-koa-peat-makes-history-with-his-3rd-usa-basketball-gold-medal/74321803007/|title=Perry's Koa Peat makes history, powers USA Basketball U17 to gold-medal win over Italy|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]|first=Richard|last=Obert|date=July 7, 2024|access-date=January 10, 2026}}</ref>

Peat helped the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States national under-19 team]] to a gold medal at the [[2025 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2025 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] in Switzerland, where he averaged 12.6 points 6.9 rebounds and 1.1 assists per game. He became the first player in [[USA Basketball]] history to win four men's international gold medals at the junior level, as well as the first player in men's basketball history to win three junior World Cup gold medals.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://arizonawildcats.com/news/2025/7/6/mens-basketball-lloyd-peat-bring-home-gold-from-fiba-u19-world-cup.aspx|title=Lloyd, Peat Bring Home Gold From FIBA U19 World Cup|publisher=[[Arizona Wildcats]]|date=July 6, 2025|access-date=January 10, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Peat was born in [[Gilbert, Arizona]].<ref name="usab">{{cite web|url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/p/peat-koa.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220706182314/https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/p/peat-koa.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 6, 2022|title=Koa Peat|publisher=[[USA Basketball]]|access-date=May 10, 2023}}</ref> He is the youngest of seven children of former [[National Football League]] (NFL) offensive guard [[Todd Peat]], who played nine seasons with the [[St. Louis Cardinals (NFL)|St. Louis]]/[[Arizona Cardinals|Phoenix Cardinals]] and [[Los Angeles Raiders]], and Jana Peat,<ref name="wrangler">{{cite news|url=https://www.wranglernews.com/2021/02/23/a-re-peat-performance-latest-in-athletic-family-is-6-7-at-14-and-rising/|title=A re-Peat performance: Latest in athletic family is 6-7 at 14, and rising|work=Wrangler News|first=Sam|last=Voas|date=February 23, 2021|access-date=May 9, 2023|archive-date=May 11, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230511155949/https://www.wranglernews.com/2021/02/23/a-re-peat-performance-latest-in-athletic-family-is-6-7-at-14-and-rising/|url-status=dead}}</ref> who played basketball, volleyball and softball in high school.<ref name="Bio">{{cite web|url=https://arizonawildcats.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/koa-peat/18561|title=Koa Peat|publisher=[[Arizona Wildcats]]|access-date=November 4, 2025}}</ref> His oldest brother, Todd Jr., played [[college football]] at [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska]], [[Eastern Arizona College|Eastern Arizona]] and [[East Texas A&M Lions football|Texas A&M–Commerce]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://lionathletics.com/sports/football/roster/todd-peat/2259|title=Todd Peat - Football - East A&M University Athletics|website=East Texas A&M University Athletics|access-date=May 9, 2023}}</ref> Another older brother, [[Andrus Peat|Andrus]], played in the NFL for the [[New Orleans Saints]], [[Las Vegas Raiders]], and [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref name=wrangler/> Another older brother, Cassius, played college football for [[Michigan State Spartans football|Michigan State]], Eastern Arizona, [[Pima Community College|Pima CC]], [[Scottsdale Community College|Scottsdale CC]] and [[Virginia Cavaliers football|Virginia]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lansingstatejournal.com/story/sports/college/msu/football/2018/06/04/cassius-peat-michigan-state-virginia-football/669379002/|title=The curious case of Cassius Peat: Former Michigan State player transfers to Virginia|work=[[Lansing State Journal]]|first=Phil|last=Friend|date=June 4, 2018|access-date=May 9, 2023}}</ref> His brother Keona also plays football for the [[Arizona Wildcats football|University of Arizona]]. His sister Leilani played [[women's college basketball]] for [[Seattle Redhawks women's basketball|Seattle]] and [[San Francisco Dons women's basketball|San Francisco]] and his sister Maya played the same sport for [[Arkansas–Pine Bluff Golden Lions women's basketball|Arkansas–Pine Bluff]] and [[Texas Tech University]].<ref name=usab/>

Peat is of [[Native Hawaiian]] descent through his mother, and his first name means "strong warrior" in the [[Hawaiian language]].<ref name=Bio/> While in high school, he volunteered on the [[Gila River Indian Community]], as well as a youth basketball and football coach.<ref name=Gatorade/>
